title: The Prophet's character ﷺ
hook: You've learned how he prayed. Today: how he treated people, especially people who hurt him.

screens.text: On Day 15 you met the Prophet ﷺ. Since then you've prayed the way he taught, maybe hundreds of times. Today is about his mercy: the moments when he could have been harsh, and wasn't.
**Sent as a mercy.** Allah says He sent the Prophet ﷺ *"as a mercy to the worlds"* [Q 21:107, Saheeh Intl.], and praised his character as great [Q 68:4].
bubbles: The Qur'an also tells him that his gentleness is what kept people close: had he been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have walked away [Q 3:159].
Mercy wasn't a side feature. It was the method.

screens.text: Tap through five moments when he could have been harsh, and wasn't.

events.title: Rejected and driven out
events.text: A town rejected him. Jibril brought an angel who offered to crush it between two mountains. He said no: he hoped their children would one day worship Allah [Bukhari 3231].

events.title: A man scoffs
events.text: A man saw him kiss his grandson and said he'd never kissed any of his ten children. He said whoever shows no mercy won't be shown mercy [Bukhari 5997].

events.title: Insulted, and calm
events.text: Visitors twisted their greeting into an insult, and his wife Aisha snapped back. He calmed her: Allah loves gentleness in every matter. He replied with two words and moved on [Bukhari 6024].

events.title: A Jewish man's funeral
events.text: He stood up out of respect. When someone pointed out whose funeral it was, he said: wasn't he a human soul? [Bukhari 1312]

events.title: No revenge for himself
events.text: Aisha said he never took revenge for himself, and when given two choices he picked the easier one, unless it was a sin [Bukhari 3560].

screens.prompt: Match each moment to what it shows.

pairs.right: Show mercy, and you'll be shown mercy

pairs.left: Answering the insult in two words
pairs.right: Allah loves gentleness in every matter

screens.text: **Gentle isn't weak.** He was firm about right and wrong, and he stood up when Allah's limits were crossed [Bukhari 3560]. But for himself, he forgave.
bubbles: That balance is hard. It's also why people trusted him: they knew his anger was never about his ego.

screens.prompt: A coworker makes a snide comment about Muslims in front of Destiny. Following the Prophet's example ﷺ, what fits best?

options.text: Stay calm, answer briefly and kindly, and don't hold a grudge
options.feedback: Yes. He answered insults with calm and dignity, and never took revenge for himself [Bukhari 3560].

options.text: Fire back with a sharper insult
options.feedback: Not quite. When Aisha fired back, he told her Allah loves gentleness in every matter [Bukhari 6024].

options.text: Stay silent, but hold it against him for months
options.feedback: Not quite. Calm on the outside is good, but he didn't carry revenge inside either.

screens.text: **Why this matters for you.** You're often the first Muslim people get to know well. Your coworkers, classmates and family won't read hadith collections. They'll read you.
bubbles: You don't need to be perfect. Pick one of his habits and practice it: a kind greeting, a calm reply, a little extra patience.

options.feedback: Right [Bukhari 3231]. Mercy, even on one of his hardest days.

options.text: Accepted, because they had hurt him
options.feedback: Not quite. He refused and hoped for their descendants' guidance [Bukhari 3231].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- He was sent as a mercy to the worlds [Q 21:107]; his character is great [Q 68:4]; his gentleness was a mercy from Allah, and harshness would have driven people away [Q 3:159].
- After being rejected (Ibn 'Abd Yalil, of the people of Ta'if), he refused the angel of the mountains' offer to destroy them, hoping their descendants would worship Allah [Bukhari 3231]. The hadith itself names the man, not the town; "a town rejected him" is how the lesson describes it.
- "Whoever is not merciful will not be shown mercy," said when he kissed his grandson al-Hasan [Bukhari 5997].
- When visitors greeted him with "as-samu 'alaykum" (death be upon you), he replied only "and upon you," and told Aisha that Allah loves gentleness in all matters [Bukhari 6024]. Don't use this story to speak badly of Jews; the point is his gentleness.
- He stood for a Jewish man's funeral: "Is it not a soul?" [Bukhari 1312].
- He chose the easier option unless it was sinful, and never took revenge for himself, only when Allah's limits were violated [Bukhari 3560].
- Revealed Path ch. 11 (his life and character).

**Likely questions**
- *"More stories?"* Use Day 15's (he served his family at home [Bukhari 676]; he asked a little boy about his pet bird [Bukhari 6203]) and this lesson's. Only bank references; never invent a story.
- *"How did he treat other faiths?"* Respect for human dignity (the funeral [Bukhari 1312]); keeping family ties with non-Muslim relatives (Asma' and her mother [Bukhari 2620]). Avoid contested history; offer the imam for detail.
- *"Where can I learn his life?"* A seerah class at the masjid, or a well-known beginner biography the imam recommends. Day 81 covers learning paths.

**Don't**
- Don't attribute words to him without a bank reference; don't put gists in quotes.
- Don't turn the lesson into a list of rules; keep it on character.
